thesis: Validate that INT3 real bit-packing preserves nsep+pchan's catastrophic-rescue property on Mode 1 models, not just the already-easy Mode 2 cases.

packing_quality.note: Larger than Llama-3.1-8B's 0.0002 but still effectively lossless: the real_packed ΔPPL (+0.387) is actually SLIGHTLY BETTER than simulated (+0.402) on Qwen2-7B. We interpret this as a numerical side-effect of FP16 storage of per-channel scales: Mode 1 models have outlier-dominated scales (e.g. Layer 0 K outlier 17.23x) where FP16 rounding creates slightly different but comparable results vs FP32. The FP16 rounding in Qwen2-7B's case happens to regularize the outlier scale favorably.

production_verdict.note: Mode 1 catastrophic case (naive INT4 +1382 ΔPPL) successfully rescued to +0.39 ΔPPL with real INT3 packing and 5.08x compression. This is the first demonstration that our bit-packing is lossless enough to preserve the nsep+pchan rescue on the pathological case.

memory_compression.note: Qwen2-7B's GQA 4:1 means smaller KV cache than Llama's GQA 4:1 but 8 heads. 40 MB FP16 baseline vs Llama's 92 MB baseline reflects this. Same 5.08x compression ratio on both.

key_takeaway: INT3 real bit-packing is production-quality on BOTH failure modes. Mode 1 (pathological, rescued 3500x) and Mode 2 (already clean) both achieve 5.08x compression with < 5% baseline PPL. The method generalizes across the dichotomy.
